sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Setup for the button
sections.what: Brings in the touch, text, spinner and gradient pieces, icons and theme values the button uses.
sections.why: Standard setup at the top of a component file.
sections.watch_out: The theme is imported with an alias path, unlike the relative paths in other files, so it depends on the alias being configured.

sections.name: ButtonProps
sections.title: Options for the button
sections.what: Lists the options a button accepts. Only the title and press action are required; the rest have defaults.
sections.why: Makes the button's options clear and reusable.
sections.watch_out: Only the title and press action are required; everything else falls back to a default.

sections.name: Button (part 1)
sections.title: Sizes and text color
sections.what: Sets three sizes, small, medium and large, and decides the text color: white on the primary look, indigo on the secondary and ghost looks. It also builds the loading spinner or the label.
sections.why: Likely reason: indigo text on a faint background keeps secondary buttons readable.
sections.watch_out: Loading swaps the whole label for a spinner, so the button shows no text while it is working.

sections.name: Button (part 2)
sections.title: Icon and label content
sections.what: Puts the optional icon on the left or right of the label, using the size and color chosen for the button.
sections.why: Keeps the content identical across all looks.
sections.watch_out: The icon and text share one color, so they always match each other.

sections.name: Button: if
sections.title: Primary button with gradient
sections.what: Draws the primary button with a blue-to-purple gradient, a slight shrink and fade while pressed, and a faded look when disabled.
sections.why: Likely reason: the main action gets the strongest look.
sections.watch_out: The gradient is always drawn; no option turns it off.

sections.name: Button (part 4)
sections.title: Other button looks and styles
sections.what: Draws the secondary, ghost, danger and success looks as flat or outlined buttons, with the same press and disabled behavior as the primary one. Also holds the styles shared by all looks.
sections.why: Likely reason: lighter looks are used for less important actions.
sections.watch_out: The danger and success text colors are defined here but never applied, so those labels stay white as set in the content section.

summary: The app's standard button, with five looks, three sizes, an optional icon, a loading spinner and a disabled state.
purpose: Gives every screen one consistent button for user actions.
why: Likely reason: one shared button keeps the look and press feedback the same everywhere.
how: Picks the size and look from the options, builds the content (spinner, text and icon), then draws either the gradient primary button or a flat button for the other looks. Pressing shrinks it slightly and fades it.
inputs: Title, press action, look (primary, secondary, ghost, danger, success), size, optional icon and its side, loading, disabled, full width and extra style.
outputs: A pressable button. Runs the press action when tapped, unless the button is disabled or loading.
risks: The danger and success text colors are defined but never applied, so their labels stay white. Loading hides the label. The file mixes a relative and an alias import path.
debug: If a button ignores taps, check whether it is disabled or loading. If a danger or success label looks wrong, see the note about unused text colors. If the import fails, check that the @ path alias is set up in the project.
